title: 2026 United States House of Representatives Election in Delaware's At-Large Congressional District
description: The 2026 election for Delaware's sole seat in the U.S. House of Representatives features first-term Democratic incumbent Sarah McBride, the first openly transgender member of Congress, facing Republican challenger Reverend Earl Cooper, a pastor and community advocate. McBride won the seat in 2024 with 57.9% of the vote after succeeding Senator Lisa Blunt Rochester. The primary elections are scheduled for September 15, 2026, and the general election on November 3, 2026. Delaware's at-large district has consistently elected Democrats; the seat is rated as Solid Democratic by nonpartisan forecasters.
polling_note: No public opinion polls were found for the 2026 Delaware U.S. House race as of mid-June 2026. The Cook Political Report rates the race as D+50, indicating a safe Democratic seat.

candidates.name: Sarah McBride
candidates.summary: Sarah McBride is an American politician, author, and LGBTQ rights activist serving as the U.S. Representative for Delaware's at-large congressional district since January 2025. She previously served in the Delaware Senate from 2021 to 2025 and was national press secretary of the Human Rights Campaign. McBride is the highest-ranking openly transgender elected official in the United States and the first openly transgender member of Congress.

candidates.name: Earl Cooper
candidates.summary: Earl L. Cooper, also known as Reverend Earl Cooper, is a Republican candidate for U.S. House in Delaware's at-large district. He is a pastor and community leader who launched a Housing Pilot Program addressing unemployment and economic disparity, and was named 2024 Minority-owned business champion of the year. Cooper previously ran as a Democrat in the 2024 primary for the same seat, receiving 16.2% of the vote.

forecast.rationale: No public polling exists for this race, reducing quantitative certainty. However, the fundamentals are exceptionally strong for Democrats: Delaware's at-large district has a Cook PVI of D+50 and is described as Solid Democratic; incumbent Sarah McBride won the seat in 2024 with 57.9% of the vote; the district has consistently elected Democrats at the federal level; and Republican challenger Earl Cooper is a first-time general-election candidate who previously ran as a Democrat in the 2024 primary and received only 16.2%. Absent any countervailing polling evidence, Democrats hold an overwhelming structural advantage. Confidence is set to medium because the forecast relies entirely on fundamentals and historical signals rather than current race-specific polling.
